fields.aka: Puruṣottama Ācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Svarūpa Gosāi
fields.disappearance: Āṣāḍha Śukla Dvitīyā, the day of Ratha-yātrā (one text: the second day after the full moon of Āṣāḍha)
fields.place: Bhiṭādiyā (family); born and raised in Navadvīpa; later Purī (Nīlācala) with Lord Caitanya
fields.works: Kaḍacā (notes on the pastimes of Lord Caitanya)
fields.notes:
Before sannyāsa: Puruṣottama Ācārya of Navadvīpa. Sannyāsa in Vārāṇasī from Caitanyānanda Bhāratī, as a naiṣṭhika-brahmacārī without saffron cloth; the name Dāmodara was added by Lord Caitanya. One of the 'three and a half' closest associates of the Lord; examined every writing before it was presented to Him; sang like a Gandharva. Father: Padmagarbha Ācārya (disciple of Lakṣmīpati). Maternal grandfather: Jayarāma Cakravartī. Half-brother: Lakṣmīnātha Lāhiḍī.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Lalitā Sakhī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 160; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). The record's text gave Viśākhā, and Lalitā according to Dhyānacandra Gosvāmī. The Sakhā-nirṇayāmṛta (37) counts him in Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch.

fields.appearance: Probably in the last part of the 1300s Śaka, near Cuttack (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna)
fields.disappearance: Jyaiṣṭha Kṛṣṇa Pañcamī (others: Vaiśākha Kṛṣṇa Pañcamī; Abhidhāna: gauṇa Vaiśākha Kṛṣṇa Pañcamī, 1455 or 1456 Śaka)
fields.place: Born near Cuttack; Vidyānagara on the Godāvarī (governor under King Pratāparudra); later Purī
fields.notes:
Father: Bhavānanda Rāya (formerly Mahārāja Pāṇḍu); mother formerly Kuntī. Brothers: Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka, Kalānidhi, Sudhānidhi, Vāṇīnātha. Minister of King Pratāparudra and governor of the Godāvarī region; met Lord Caitanya on the banks of the Godāvarī, on the recommendation of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya; their conversations are in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya 8. Born in a kāraṇa family, which he called śūdra. The Bhajana-nirṇaya calls him a disciple of Rāghavendra Purī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Viśākhā Sakhī; also Arjuna, the Pāṇḍava and Kṛṣṇa's priya-narma-sakhā, and the gopī Arjunīyā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 120-124; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Some say Lalitā, but this is not accepted by all.
Dates/place from B. V. Tīrtha, “Sri Chaitanya: His Associates”, and the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna.

fields.appearance: First part of the 1300s Śaka, in Navadvīpa (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna)
fields.place: Navadvīpa (Vidyānagara); Purī, court paṇḍita of King Pratāparudra
fields.works: Sārvabhauma-nirukta (commentary on the Tattva-cintāmaṇi); ṭīkā on the Advaita-makaranda; Śrī Caitanya-śataka; hymns of 108 names (of Caitanya, Nityānanda, Advaita, Gadādhara); Samasavāda; Sāravatī
fields.notes:
Father: Maheśvara (Narahari) Viśārada. Brother: Vidyā-vācaspati. Sister's husband: Gopīnātha Ācārya. Son: Jaleśvara Vāhinīpati. Daughter: Ṣāṭhī (husband Amogha). Studied nyāya with Pakṣadhara Miśra in Mithilā (Dīneśa Candra Bhaṭṭācārya: with his father, in Navadvīpa). Court paṇḍita of King Pratāparudra in Purī; defeated by Lord Caitanya, he became His servant (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 6).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Bṛhaspati (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 119).

Husband of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya's sister; son-in-law of Maheśvara Viśārada (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.130, Madhya 6.18). In Purī the first to proclaim Lord Caitanya as Kṛṣṇa Himself; the Lord gave him the care of the devotees from Bengal.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Brahmā; also the sakhī Ratnāvalī (v. 178) (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 75, 178).
According to BBM, Gopīnātha was a brāhmaṇa resident of Navadvīpa and did not reside at Nīlācala. He came to Purī as a Vaiṣṇava visitor from Gauḍa. He was Brahmā in his past incarnation. BBM refers to Vaiṣṇavavandanā 21 in Bengali which is identical to the verse quoted in GVA in reference to Gopīnātha Ṭhākura. (See also "Gopīnātha Ṭhākura")
